definitions: To have more than one skill, resource, or option available to you, so that if one fails, you can use another.
To have an alternative course of action or means of support.
examples: It's always good to have two strings to one's bow in a competitive job market.
She has two strings to her bow, being both a talented musician and a skilled programmer.
He felt more secure knowing he had two strings to his bow if his initial plan didn't work out.
lemma: have two strings to one's bow
source: have two strings to one's bow
